paper: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第3套
limit: at least 120 words but not more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
body: It has been proposed that every university student should be required to take part in at least one research project. In my view, the proposal is necessary, and it is also practical as long as it is carried out flexibly.

The requirement is necessary because research teaches what ordinary classes seldom can. When students design an experiment or conduct a survey, they learn to ask good questions, analyze data and solve problems on their own. Working with teachers and teammates also develops their communication skills and sense of responsibility. These gains will benefit them whether they pursue further study or enter the job market.

The proposal is also practical. Most universities already have laboratories, libraries and teachers engaged in research, so students can join existing projects instead of starting from scratch. Projects can range from a small task in a professor’s experiment to a semester-long independent survey, allowing students of all majors to find a good fit. With proper guidance and a reasonable schedule, research will be a valuable experience for students rather than a burden.

paper: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第2套
limit: at least 120 words but not more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose you are invited to put forward a proposal to the university on how to make students’ campus life easier. You are now to write an essay to make your proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
body: Campus life can be busy and sometimes stressful. Many students rush between classes, wait in long lines and struggle to find the information they need. To make their daily lives easier, I would like to propose three practical measures.

To begin with, the university could develop a single mobile app that brings together course schedules, library seat reservations, repair requests and canteen menus, so that students no longer have to visit several websites or offices. In addition, the opening hours of key facilities such as the library and the gym could be extended into the evening, when most students are free. Finally, a one-stop service center would allow students to handle paperwork, ask questions and get help in one place.

These measures would not require a large investment, yet they would save students a great deal of time and energy. With fewer daily hassles, students could focus more on their studies and enjoy a richer campus life. I sincerely hope the university will give this proposal serious consideration.

paper: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第1套
limit: at least 120 words but not more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
body: Robots are no longer the stuff of science fiction. As the technology matures, they will soon become a familiar part of campus life, taking over routine tasks and leaving students and teachers more time for what really matters.

In the near future, robots are likely to be useful in at least three areas. First, they could deliver packages and meals around campus, so students would no longer have to wait in line at pickup points. Second, robot assistants in the library could help readers locate books and put returned ones back on the right shelves. Third, in laboratories, robots could carry out dangerous or repetitive procedures with great precision, reducing risks and freeing students to focus on creative thinking.

Still, robots should serve people rather than replace them. The university needs clear rules to protect students’ privacy, and students should remember that no machine can take the place of face-to-face communication with teachers and classmates. If used wisely, robots will make our campus safer, smarter and more efficient for everyone.
